items.question: What is A1, A2, B1, B2 German?
items.answer:
German language proficiency is classified into six levels—A1, A2, B1, B2, C1, and C2—under the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR). Each level represents a different stage of German language ability:

A1 – Beginner: Learn basic German words and phrases, introduce yourself, ask simple questions, and handle common everyday situations.

A2 – Elementary: Communicate in familiar situations, understand simple conversations, and talk about everyday topics such as family, work, shopping, and routine activities.

B1 – Intermediate: Communicate independently in familiar situations, express opinions, describe experiences, and understand the main points of standard German.

B2 – Upper-Intermediate: Communicate with greater fluency and confidence, discuss more complex topics, understand detailed conversations, and use German effectively for academic and professional purposes.

At Fluent AUF, you can progress through German language levels from A1 to C2 with structured courses designed to support your learning journey from beginner to advanced proficiency.

items.question: Can I learn German in 3 months?
items.answer:
Yes, you can learn German in 3 months, although the level achieved will vary based on your current ability, study hours, and consistency.

Using Fluent AUF, a dedicated 3-month study program can help you establish a good base of German language proficiency, especially at A1 level. By attending regular German classes, speaking exercises, vocabulary building, and daily self-study, you can achieve basic competency in German and converse easily in daily situations.

To make quick progress, you should try to:

  • Attend regular German classes.
  • Speak German daily.
  • Acquire vocabulary daily.
  • Listen to German audio and video content.
  • Read and write in German.
  • Take mock tests to measure your progress.
